mappings.note: Rows A, B and C identify solid, gas and liquid by speed (LO-3); row D is a zero that only the vacuum outcome LO-4 explains.
What actually travels is the disturbance - LO-5. Same outcome as O9 and openly so; the two are the same question asked twice.

The chain starts at the vocal cords (LO-1) and runs through particle oscillation and energy propagation (LO-5). The eardrum step has no outcome in this frame, which is recorded as a gap rather than mapped.
The reciprocal relation between frequency and time period: two of the characteristics LO-6 lists, and nothing else.

Wavelength is an LO-6 characteristic, but the key defines it between consecutive COMPRESSIONS, which needs LO-5's longitudinal picture. That is what separates it from V73's plain crest-to-crest definition.

SONAR has no outcome (CG2); the second half of the key is the ULTRASONIC classification, which is a frequency band and so LO-6. Not LO-79: nothing is calculated, the depth is only identified on a diagram.
One-step v = f-lambda substitution. LO-6 for the characteristics, LO-79 for the prediction.
Statement 1 is dependence on the state of the medium (LO-3); statements 2 and 3 are temperature and humidity, which change the speed within one medium and so fall to LO-6.
Solid faster than gas, with the solid/liquid/gas ordering as the reason - LO-3 exactly. No process code: nothing is computed or modelled.
Ascending order across the three states. Shares LO-3 with O31 and honestly so - the frame has one outcome for 'travels through different mediums' and these are two drills on it.
Pitch as the perception of frequency: LO-73 for the perceptual half, LO-6 for the physical quantity.

Loudness as the perception of amplitude. Same code pair as O33 because LO-73 fuses 'loudness and pitch' into one row - the frame cannot separate the two, and that is a defect rather than a mapping choice.
Unlike O33 this one must COMPUTE four frequencies from counts and times before answering, so LO-79 joins LO-6, with LO-73 for the pitch framing.

Timbre. No learning outcome mentions sound quality, but competency C2.7's own text says 'differences in what we hear as it propagates through different instruments', which is exactly this. LO-73 for the music context.
d = vt on the speed of sound. LO-6 owns speed; LO-79 the substitution. Not LO-77: the item asks only for the distance, not for the factors behind the delay.
Statement 1 is the solid-versus-gas comparison (LO-3); statements 2, 3 and 4 are temperature, a numeric speed in air and humidity, all LO-6.
Three things at once: frequency and amplitude values (LO-6), loudness as perception (LO-73), and the audible range, which no outcome states and which CG2 has to carry.

A tone as a single frequency is a music-theory distinction, so LO-73 with its parent C5.3, whose text names 'sound pitch, octave, and amplitude in music'. Not LO-6: the item is about the musical category, not about measuring frequency.

Asks WHY temperature raises the speed, i.e. identify the factor governing a phenomenon - LO-77 - with LO-6 for speed itself. That reason-seeking is what separates it from O30 and O38, which only sort true from false.

Sa-Re-Ga-Ma is Indian classical notation, so this is the one music item where LO-74 under C6.1 (India's contributions) is the right sibling rather than LO-73 under C5.3. LO-6 for the ascending frequency itself.
The 20 Hz to 20 kHz audible range is a fact about human hearing that no outcome states - CG2 - with LO-6 for the frequency quantity. Flagged as a genuine frame gap.
Four scenarios must each be run through t = 2d/v and tested against 0.1 s: LO-79 for the repeated prediction, CG2 because the echo condition itself has no outcome.

Pure ear anatomy - the cochlea's transduction role. Nothing in curriculum 82's legal set for this chapter names the ear, so CG2 is cited alone rather than stretching LO-73 or C2.7. Recorded as a poor fit.
Binaural localisation. Again no outcome covers hearing anatomy or the brain's processing of it; a single honest goal-level code rather than an invented fit.
The answer is the name of a diagnostic test (audiogram). Neither noise-induced hearing loss nor audiometry appears anywhere in the frame; cited at goal level and recorded as a poor fit.
